1.g3 Nf6 2.Bg2.strategy: Completes the fianchetto: the bishop eyes the centre and b7 along the long diagonal, and the king is one step from castling. The cost is that White still holds no central square, so Black is free to claim space with pawns and White must prove later that the bishop's pressure counts for more.

1.g3 Nf6 2.Nf3.strategy: Develops a knight towards the centre and covers e5, so Black cannot simply occupy it. It prepares quick castling and keeps White's pawn structure flexible, but White still has no pawn in the centre and the game stays quiet and manoeuvring, with Black free to take space.

1.g3 Nf6 2.c4.strategy: Fights for d5 from the flank and keeps both knights and the d-pawn free to choose their squares. The aim is pressure on the centre rather than occupying it, which asks for patience: Black may take space, and White must undermine it later with the fianchettoed bishop and pawn breaks.

1.g3 Nf6 2.d4.strategy: Takes the centre with a pawn and opens the way for the bishop and quick development. It is sound, but commits the d-pawn before Black's set-up is clear, and Black can challenge the centre at once.

1.g3 Nf6 2.d3.strategy: Supports e4 and frees the c1-bishop for a quiet set-up around the fianchettoed bishop. It is sound but modest: Black takes the centre at once, and White's game stays passive until e4 can be played.

1.g3 Nf6 2.Nc3.strategy: Develops the knight, covers d5 and e4 and supports a later e4. It blocks the c-pawn, though, so English and Catalan plans with c4 are off for now, and Black can take space at once and drive the knight away with a pawn.

1.g3 Nf6 2.c3.strategy: Prepares d4 with a solid pawn chain, but develops nothing and takes c3 from the queen's knight. The pawn does not fight for d5, so Black takes the centre with ...d5 and develops freely.

1.g3 Nf6 2.e3.strategy: Supports d4 and prepares a quiet set-up. It is sound but passive: once d4 follows, the e3-pawn shuts in the c1-bishop, which then needs b3 to come out, and Black takes the centre at once.

1.g3 Nf6 2.b3.strategy: Prepares Bb2, so that with Bg2 both bishops bear on the centre from the long diagonals. It is sound but slow in the centre: Black can claim central space at once or contest the long diagonal with a fianchetto of its own.

1.g3 Nf6 2.f4.strategy: Controls e5 and aims for an attack on the kingside, like a Dutch Defence with colours reversed. It is sound but loosens the king's position: with the f-pawn gone, the g1–a7 diagonal lies open towards a castled king, and Black takes the centre at once.

1.g3 Nf6 2.Nh3.strategy: Develops the knight to the rim, where it keeps the f-pawn free and can go to f4, but covers no central square. Black takes the centre at once, and Nf3 would develop the same piece to a better square.

1.g3 Nf6 2.Bh3.strategy: Develops the bishop on the c8–h3 diagonal instead of fianchettoing it. Once Black frees the light-squared bishop, it faces it, and either the bishops are traded, leaving the light squares weakened by g3 without their defender, or White retreats to g2 a tempo down.

1.g3 Nf6 2.Na3.strategy: Develops the knight to the rim, where it eyes b5 and c4 but guards nothing in the centre. Black takes the centre with ...d5, which also covers c4, and the same piece would do more on c3.

1.g3 Nf6 2.b4.strategy: Grabs queenside space and prepares Bb2, but nothing defends the pawn: after ...e6 the f8-bishop attacks it, and White must spend another tempo defending it or give it up. Black meanwhile takes the centre.

1.g3 Nf6 2.a3.strategy: Spends a tempo on a queenside pawn move that prepares b4 but does nothing for the centre or development. Black takes space in the centre at once.

1.g3 Nf6 2.a4.strategy: Gains queenside space and controls b5, but spends a tempo on a rim pawn that does nothing for the centre or development. Black occupies the centre at once and develops freely.

1.g3 Nf6 2.f3.strategy: Prepares e4, but takes f3 from the g1-knight, blocks the long diagonal the g3 fianchetto was meant to open and loosens the g1–a7 diagonal. Black takes the centre at once.

1.g3 Nf6 2.h3.strategy: A waiting move that stops ...Ng4 and ...Bg4 but costs a tempo with the centre and development untouched. Black takes the centre at once while White has nothing to show for it.

1.g3 Nf6 2.h4.strategy: Gains kingside space for h5, but with no ...g6 to attack yet it spends a tempo on a rim pawn while the centre and development wait. It also loosens the pawns in front of White's own king, and Black takes the centre at once.

1.g3 Nf6 2.g4.strategy: Hangs a pawn: nothing defends g4, so 2...Nxg4 wins it for free, and the kingside is left weakened.

1.g3 Nf6 2.e4.strategy: Leaves the e-pawn undefended: after 2...Nxe4 3.Bg2 attacks the knight, but ...d5 holds it, and Black keeps a clean extra pawn.

1.g3 Nf6 2.Bg2 d5.strategy: Claims the centre with a pawn, the natural fit for the knight on f6. The d5-pawn becomes the target of White's bishop and queenside pawns, but in return Black has space and a sound game. A strategic fight over d5 and the long diagonal, usually without early fireworks.

1.g3 Nf6 2.Bg2 g6.strategy: Copies White's set-up: the bishop will rule the long diagonal a1–h8 and the king castles behind it. Black builds from a distance and leaves the centre unsettled, so White chooses the structure. A slow, manoeuvring game with both long diagonals in play.

1.g3 Nf6 2.Bg2 e5.strategy: Takes space in the centre with a pawn and opens the f8-bishop. The pawn needs support as soon as a knight attacks it, which is the price of the space. White's bishop on g2 watches the centre, so the game is a fight over the centre rather than a quiet build-up.

1.g3 Nf6 2.Bg2 c5.strategy: Controls d4 from the flank instead of occupying the centre, and keeps every set-up open. The cost is that Black claims no central square yet, so White may take space first. A flexible game that is decided by manoeuvring more than by early contact.

1.g3 Nf6 2.Bg2 e6.strategy: Opens the f8-bishop and prepares ...d5 for a solid set-up. The cost is the c8-bishop, which stays shut in behind the pawn once ...d5 follows and has to be freed later. A quiet game with a sound structure and little risk.

1.g3 Nf6 2.Bg2 Nc6.strategy: Develops a knight towards d4 and e5 and blocks the long diagonal, so Bxc6 would only give up White's best bishop. It puts no pawn in the centre, though, so White can take space with d4 or c4 and Black must react. Sound, but less flexible than …d5 or …e5.

1.g3 Nf6 2.Bg2 c6.strategy: Prepares …d5 behind a solid pawn chain and closes the long diagonal in advance. The c-pawn is committed before White shows a set-up, and the b8-knight loses c6 and usually develops via d7. Sound, but slower than …d5 at once.

1.g3 Nf6 2.Bg2 d6.strategy: Prepares ...e5 and a compact set-up, and opens the c8-bishop's diagonal. It concedes central space, so White can build a broad pawn centre. Sound, though passive.

1.g3 Nf6 2.Bg2 Na6.strategy: Puts a knight on the rim, from where it eyes b4 and c5 but does nothing for the centre. White gets time to develop and take the centre, and a pawn on d4 would also take c5 away.

1.g3 Nf6 2.Bg2 Rg8.strategy: Wastes a tempo and gives up kingside castling for good, without helping development or the centre. The rook has no job on g8, and White simply develops.

1.g3 Nf6 2.Bg2 a6.strategy: A waiting move that prepares ...b5, but that advance would still drop the a8-rook to Bxa8 while the long diagonal is open. It does nothing for the centre or development.

1.g3 Nf6 2.Bg2 a5.strategy: Gains a little queenside space and takes b4 from White's pieces. It is sound and costs nothing at once, but it does nothing for the centre or development, so White develops with a free hand.

1.g3 Nf6 2.Bg2 g5.strategy: Gains kingside space but loosens f5 and h5 and the cover of a future castled king. The pawn is also exposed: 3.d4 threatens Bxg5 and 3.h4 attacks it directly, so Black must spend further moves on it.

1.g3 Nf6 2.Bg2 h6.strategy: Takes g5 away from the c1 bishop before it is even free. The move is sound and costs little, but it develops nothing and puts no pawn in the centre, so White claims the centre first.

1.g3 Nf6 2.Bg2 h5.strategy: Prepares ...h4 to open lines against g3, but weakens g5 and develops nothing. White can stop the pawn with h4 or simply develop.

1.g3 Nf6 2.Bg2 Ng8.strategy: Undoes the first move. Black has spent two tempi to get back to the start while White has developed the bishop and keeps a free hand in the centre.

1.g3 Nf6 2.Bg2 Ng4.strategy: Eyes f2 and h2, but both are guarded and 3.h3 drives the knight away at once; a retreat to e5 only gains White more time, as the knight is attacked again. After the retreat to f6 Black has spent two moves on the knight while White has added h3.

1.g3 Nf6 2.Bg2 Nh5.strategy: Puts the knight on the rim, where it eyes g3 but cannot take it, as the pawn is guarded by h2 and f2. It does nothing for the centre or development, and White gets a free move.

1.g3 Nf6 2.Bg2 b6.strategy: Opens the long diagonal, and 3.Bxa8 takes the rook, as nothing recaptures on a8; even if the bishop is later trapped there, White stays at least the exchange ahead. A queenside fianchetto works only after the diagonal is closed first, for instance by …d5 or …c6.

1.g3 Nf6 2.Bg2 b5.strategy: Opens the long diagonal as well: 3.Bxa8 takes the rook, since nothing recaptures on a8, and White stays at least the exchange ahead even if the bishop is later trapped there. The queenside space gained does not make up for the material.

1.g3 Nf6 2.Bg2 Ne4.strategy: Walks into the bishop's diagonal: 3.Bxe4 wins the knight, as nothing guards e4 and Black has no pawn on d5 to recapture.

1.g3 Nf6 2.Bg2 Nd5.strategy: Hangs the knight: 3.Bxd5 wins it, since the d7-pawn blocks the queen from recapturing on d5 and nothing else guards the square.
